name: sol_defi_as_7
description: Missing slippage protection in swap/trade functions allowing excessive price deviation losses
question: The source file in `source` implements a swap, trade, or liquidity function that executes a token exchange or transfer based on a computed or pool-derived output amount without accepting and enforcing a caller-supplied minimum output (or maximum input) parameter, so a trade can execute at an arbitrarily worse price than expected due to price movement, front-running, or sandwich attacks, causing unexpected loss to the user; this excludes functions that accept and revert on violation of a minAmountOut/maxAmountIn or equivalent slippage/deadline bound, and excludes non-trading functions such as admin configuration or view/query functions.
criteria: swap() computes amountOut from reserves and transfers it to the user without comparing it to any user-supplied minAmountOut
A liquidity removal function calculates token amounts from pool share and sends them without checking against a minimum amount parameter
A trade function accepts amountIn and executes the exchange at the current pool price with no minOut or maxSlippage argument at all
A router-style function forwards swap calls to a pool contract without passing through or validating any slippage bound provided by the caller
